From Puckline Press

Puckline Press article

Frozen Frenzy, explained: the night all 32 NHL teams play

Tuesday's 16-game Frozen Frenzy was the fourth in a row. Here's what the event is, where it came from, how rare it is, and how last night went.

By Puckline Prince · Oct 14, 2026 · Article page

Read the article

Every NHL team played on Tuesday night. That's the Frozen Frenzy: one evening, 16 games, all 32 clubs, and a new puck drop almost every 15 minutes from 6 p.m. Eastern until the last game started at 11. ESPN says this was the fourth year in a row it has put the event on.

The Frozen Frenzy is a scheduling showcase built with ESPN. The league gives the night a full slate, then spreads the start times out so the games overlap as little as possible. ESPN carries a tripleheader on its main channel (6 p.m., 8:30 p.m. and 11 p.m. Eastern), and the other 13 games stream on its services.

The centrepiece is a whip-around studio show that jumps from rink to rink for goals, big hits and late finishes, the hockey version of the NFL's RedZone. In the first edition, John Buccigross and Kevin Weekes hosted it, and the show ran about six and a half hours across ESPN+ and ESPN2.

This year's tripleheader was Devils at Red Wings at 6, Avalanche at Stars at 8:30 and Bruins at Sharks at 11. The other games started every 15 minutes from 6:15 to 9 p.m., then at 9:45 (Flames at Ducks) and 10:30 (Oilers at Kings), so all 16 games had their own start time.

A night with all 32 teams in action is newer than you might think. The first 16-game day in NHL history was Saturday, April 8, 2023, the last Saturday of the 2022-23 regular season. That day started at 12:30 p.m. Eastern and was not branded as anything.

The first Frozen Frenzy came six months later, on Tuesday, Oct. 24, 2023. NHL.com called it the second 16-game day in league history. ESPN's tripleheader that night was Maple Leafs at Capitals, Bruins at Blackhawks (Connor Bedard's rookie season) and Flyers at the Golden Knights, the defending Stanley Cup champions.

Since then it has become a fixture of October:

  • Oct. 24, 2023: the first Frozen Frenzy
  • Oct. 22, 2024: opened with Capitals at Flyers, closed with Kings at Golden Knights
  • Oct. 28, 2025: opened with Penguins at Flyers, closed with Kings at Sharks
  • Oct. 13, 2026: opened with Devils at Red Wings, closed with Bruins at Sharks

All four have been on a Tuesday.

Nights like this are rare. Before the 2024 edition, NHL.com counted only three earlier days with all 32 teams playing: April 8, 2023, the first Frozen Frenzy, and Jan. 13, 2024. It also said the 2024 Frenzy would be the only day that season with every team in action.

So the Frenzy is the one guaranteed 16-game night on the calendar, and in some seasons it has been the only one.

The 2026 edition delivered 112 goals in 16 games, an average of seven a game. Road teams won nine of the 16. Three games went past regulation: the Devils won in overtime in Detroit, 5-4, and the Canadiens (over Buffalo, 4-3) and Kraken (in Philadelphia, 3-2) both won in shootouts.

All the final scores:

  • Devils 5, Red Wings 4 (OT)
  • Panthers 7, Blue Jackets 3
  • Canadiens 4, Sabres 3 (SO)
  • Hurricanes 4, Capitals 2
  • Kraken 3, Flyers 2 (SO)
  • Rangers 4, Lightning 1
  • Blues 7, Senators 2
  • Islanders 3, Canucks 2
  • Blackhawks 5, Penguins 3
  • Jets 5, Wild 2
  • Avalanche 3, Stars 2
  • Golden Knights 5, Predators 2
  • Mammoth 5, Maple Leafs 4
  • Flames 4, Ducks 2
  • Oilers 4, Kings 1
  • Bruins 6, Sharks 3

The most lopsided results were Florida's 7-3 win in Columbus and St. Louis's 7-2 win in Ottawa. In the 8:30 headliner, Colorado beat Dallas 3-2 in regulation, and Boston closed the night with six goals in San Jose.

Full recaps of every game are on the Last night page.

Thursday, October 29

Game recap

PHI2WSH5Final: PHI 2, WSH 5

Dylan Strome handed out treats a few days early: three assists, all of them gift-wrapped for Alex Tuch and Jordan Kyrou in a 5-2 Capitals win over Philadelphia. Tuch opened the scoring 1:50 in and closed it with an empty-netter, two goals on the night. Kyrou also scored twice, a power-play goal in the second and the one that put Washington back up two after Matvei Michkov's power-play goal made it 3-2 midway through the third. Sean Couturier had the other Flyers goal, and Aliaksei Protas got his first of the season. Logan Thompson stopped 23 of 25; Joseph Woll stopped 25 of 29. Matt Roy threw nine hits and still found time for an assist. Washington is 7-4-0. Philadelphia is 3-8-4, and two goals is starting to look less like a bad night and more like the ceiling.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

CGY0EDM4Final: CGY 0, EDM 4

The Battle of Alberta lasted about one period. Mathieu Joseph scored at 7:46 of the first off a Connor McDavid feed, Mattias Ekholm made it 2-0 in the second, and then Edmonton scored twice in 21 seconds early in the third: Kasperi Kapanen on the power play and Alex Formenton right behind him. McDavid and Ryan Nugent-Hopkins had two assists each, and Tristan Jarry stopped all 24 shots for the shutout. Calgary tried a goalie change after the first, with Devin Cooley (8 saves on 9) giving way to Dustin Wolf (20 on 23), which fixed nothing because the problem was at the other end. Ty Emberson and Brennan Othmann dropped the gloves in the first. Edmonton is 9-2-2. Calgary is 5-7-0 and used two goalies and zero goals, which is a lot of equipment for a night with nothing to show for it.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

NJD2COL5Final: NJD 2, COL 5

Connor Brown scored both New Jersey goals, including an unassisted shorthanded one in the first, and the Devils still got run over 5-2 in Denver. Colorado scored five straight: Gabriel Landeskog tied it on the power play in the second, then Nazem Kadri, Parker Kelly, Nathan MacKinnon and Jaden Schwartz piled on in the third, the last two 30 seconds apart. Brent Burns and Sam Malinski had two assists each, and Kadri and Schwartz had a goal and an assist. The Avalanche outshot New Jersey 44-22; Jake Allen made 39 saves, Mackenzie Blackwood 20. Colorado is 7-5-1. New Jersey is 8-5-0, and after trading for a Vezina goalie last week, the 44 shots suggest the next phone call should be about the defense.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

TOR4SEA5Final: TOR 4, SEA 5

Toronto did the hard part and then forgot to finish. Down 4-2 in the third, the Leafs got one from Jack Roslovic and a 6-on-5 tying goal from Auston Matthews with 1:30 left, and then Brandon Montour won it for Seattle with 33 seconds to go, 5-4. Gavin McKenna had his first two-goal game, both on the power play, plus an assist; Matthews had a goal and two assists. Seattle spread it around: Berkly Catton, Josh Mahura with his first of the season, Chandler Stephenson on the power play, Ryker Evans and Montour, with Mackie Samoskevich adding two assists. Sergei Bobrovsky stopped 12 of 17; Philipp Grubauer 18 of 22. Cale Fleury and Vinni Lettieri fought in the second. Seattle is 8-4-1. Toronto is 7-6-2 and erased a two-goal deficit only to lose in the last minute, which is the most Maple Leafs sentence ever written.

Wednesday, October 28

Game recap

CBJ4PHI3OTFinal: CBJ 4, PHI 3 OT

Columbus scored three goals in 2:46 of the first period, then spent the next 40 minutes trying to give them back, and the Flyers almost took the gift. Adam Fantilli, Kent Johnson and Denton Mateychuk built the 3-0 lead on a Dan Vladar who finished with 11 saves on 15 shots, which is a lot of goals for a team that only managed 15 shots all night. Noah Cates and Trevor Zegras chipped away, and Jamie Drysdale tied it with the goalie pulled and 11 seconds left. Then Johnson, with two goals and an assist, ended it 2:22 into overtime. Cam Talbot made 28 saves for the Blue Jackets. Philadelphia outshot Columbus 31-15 and still lost, now 0-3 in 3-on-3 overtime, the hockey version of running a marathon and missing the finish line by a step. The Flyers keep finding new ways to lose, and they're getting creative about it.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

BOS1CAR2Final: BOS 1, CAR 2

The Bruins scored 91 seconds in, on a Pavel Zacha power-play goal, and then apparently decided that was plenty. Boston managed 15 shots all night. Carolina had 30, and Jeremy Swayman (28 saves) kept it close until the Hurricanes finally solved him. Jackson Blake tied it with 52 seconds left in the first, and Sebastian Aho put home his eighth of the season at 10:19 of the third for the winner. Pyotr Kochetkov needed only 14 saves, which is basically a paid night off. Nicolas Deslauriers and Tanner Jeannot dropped the gloves in the first for the evening's other entertainment, and Mark Jankowski returned to the Carolina lineup. The Hurricanes move to 10-2-2. The Bruins are 9-3-1 and still good, but 15 shots against a top team is a business trip where you forget your laptop.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

LAK1CHI2Final: LAK 1, CHI 2

Chicago snapped a three-game losing streak, and it took a defenseman scoring his first of the year to do it. Samuel Helenius gave the Kings an early lead with his first goal of the season at 2:31, and Los Angeles then went the final 57 minutes without another one. Roman Kantserov tied it on a second-period power play off a Connor Bedard feed, and Wyatt Kaiser won it at 7:17 of the third, from Frank Nazar and Patrick Kane. Spencer Knight was excellent with 25 saves on 26 shots; Anton Forsberg made 25 at the other end. Quinton Byfield fired six shots and Artemi Panarin played nearly 24 minutes without a point. The Blackhawks improve to 4-8-0. The Kings fall to 3-6-2 with one goal from their fourth line and none from anybody paid to score them.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

MTL2STL0Final: MTL 2, STL 0

Jacob Fowler stopped all 46 shots the Blues threw at him, and St. Louis threw just about everything, the rink's spare pucks included. Philip Broberg had six shots, four other Blues had five each, and none of them got one past Fowler. The Canadiens needed only 20 shots of their own. Zachary Bolduc scored in the second period, Florian Xhekaj got his first of the season early in the third, and Mike Matheson assisted on both. Jordan Binnington made 18 saves and still took the loss, which won't help a goalie already sitting on the trade boards. Montreal is 7-3-2. The Blues fall to 5-6-1 after outshooting a team 46-20 and getting shut out, and at some point they have to stop blaming the goalie and start blaming the aim.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

NYI4NSH3SOFinal: NYI 4, NSH 3 SO

The Islanders led 3-0 eight minutes into the second period, and Nashville spent the rest of regulation proving that no lead in Music City is safe. Anthony Duclair, Brayden Schenn and Bo Horvat built it; Filip Forsberg (power play), Alexander Kerfoot and Ryan O'Reilly erased it, O'Reilly tying the game 4:16 into the third. Overtime solved nothing, though Matthew Schaefer played all of it and finished with 32:16 of ice time, the kind of workload usually reserved for a veteran. In the shootout Kyle Palmieri and Horvat scored, while O'Reilly and Forsberg both missed. Semyon Varlamov made 20 saves; Juuse Saros made 25. New York is 6-4-2. The Predators are 4-3-5, a team so committed to the loser point it should hang a banner for it.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

NJD5DAL1Final: NJD 5, DAL 1

Connor Hellebuyck's Devils debut was about as stressful as a warm bath: 17 saves on 18 shots, with the skaters in front of him doing everything else. Nico Hischier scored twice, opening the night at 2:41 and adding another 38 seconds into the second. Jesper Boqvist, Luke Hughes and Jack Hughes did the rest, and the Hughes brothers each had a goal. Justin Hryckowian got Dallas its only goal. Jamie Benn and Brenden Dillon fought in the second period, which was the closest the Stars came to winning anything. Casey DeSmith allowed five goals on 27 shots. New Jersey has won four straight and is 8-4-0. Dallas falls to 7-4-1 and looked like a team that had read about Hellebuyck all week and decided not to bother him.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

FLA5WPG1Final: FLA 5, WPG 1

Florida was up 3-0 before the 11-minute mark, and Winnipeg's penalty kill treated the Panthers' power play like a guest of honour. Carter Verhaeghe scored twice on the power play, Niko Mikkola added one in between, and Sam Reinhart made it three power-play goals on the night in the second. Brady Tkachuk finished it in the third, with brother Matthew assisting for his fourth helper of the night. Seth Jones had three assists. Adam Lowry's shorthanded goal was the only thing Jets fans got to cheer. Akira Schmid made 24 saves; Clay Stevenson allowed five on 24 shots. The Panthers are 7-4-2. The Jets are 4-5-3, and a penalty kill that leaky makes every Florida trip to the box look like a free shift.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

MIN3UTA1Final: MIN 3, UTA 1

Three fights and two power-play goals: the Wild brought both the fists and the finish to Utah. Liam O'Brien and Michael McCarron fought in the first, Mikhail Sergachev and Matt Boldy went 88 seconds later, and Vincent Trocheck and Danila Yurov added a third in the second. When the hockey broke out, Minnesota's power play did the damage. Joel Eriksson Ek scored in the second and Kirill Kaprizov got his 14th of the season 48 seconds into the third, both with Quinn Hughes assisting. Maxim Shabanov made it 3-0, and Logan Cooley's late 6-on-5 goal only spoiled the shutout. Jesper Wallstedt made 26 saves; Karel Vejmelka made 27. The Wild are 9-3-2. Utah is 8-5-0 and learned that winning the fights doesn't count on the scoreboard.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

OTT1VGK4Final: OTT 1, VGK 4

For almost 40 minutes nobody scored; then Vegas remembered it's the house. Braeden Bowman scored on the power play with 11 seconds left in the second, Shane Pinto answered on a power play 34 seconds into the third, and Raphael Lavoie scored his first of the season at 8:01 for the winner. William Karlsson and Jack Eichel then added empty-netters, which turns a nervy 2-1 into a 4-1 final. Adin Hill was sharp with 25 saves on 26 shots, and Jonas Johansson matched him with 25 of 27 before the empty net did the rest. Mitch Marner had an assist on Karlsson's goal. Vegas is 9-4-1. The Senators fall to 8-5-0 and flew all that way to learn the Vegas lesson: you can stay at the table a long time, but you don't walk out ahead.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

VAN6ANA5OTFinal: VAN 6, ANA 5 OT

The Canucks hadn't won in double-digit games, trailed 5-2 with under eight minutes left, and somehow won. Anaheim had this one framed: A.J. Greer scored twice, Jeff Malott, Beckett Sennecke and Leo Carlsson piled on, and it was 4-1 after two. Then Brock Boeser and Jamie Oleksiak scored, and Jonathan Lekkerimäki scored twice with the goalie pulled, at 17:14 and 18:03, to tie it. Filip Hronek won it on a power play 4:49 into overtime, his first of the season. Lukas Dostal allowed six on 33 shots; Leevi Meriläinen gave up five on 23 and still got the win. Vancouver is 3-10-1. The Ducks are 5-6-1 and found the one way to lose to a team that had forgotten how to win: give up four goals in the last 12 minutes of hockey.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

BUF2SJS0Final: BUF 2, SJS 0

Yaroslav Askarov stopped 38 of 39 shots and lost, which is the San Jose experience in one sentence. Olen Zellweger scored 50 seconds into the second period, and that was the only puck anybody got past Askarov all night. Zach Benson's first of the season went into an empty net with 55 seconds left. At the other end Colten Ellis was barely needed and perfect when he was, stopping all 23 shots for the shutout. Owen Power assisted on both Buffalo goals. The Sabres improve to 5-4-3. The Sharks fall to 6-6-1 after getting outshot 39-23 at home, and a rebuild that leaves its best player stopping 38 shots alone is a rebuild that still has a long way to go.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Puckline's Report

Dylan Strome handed out treats a few days early: three assists, all of them gift-wrapped for Alex Tuch and Jordan Kyrou in a 5-2 Capitals win over Philadelphia. Tuch opened the scoring 1:50 in and closed it with an empty-netter, two goals on the night. Kyrou also scored twice, a power-play goal in the second and the one that put Washington back up two after Matvei Michkov's power-play goal made it 3-2 midway through the third. Sean Couturier had the other Flyers goal, and Aliaksei Protas got his first of the season. Logan Thompson stopped 23 of 25; Joseph Woll stopped 25 of 29. Matt Roy threw nine hits and still found time for an assist. Washington is 7-4-0. Philadelphia is 3-8-4, and two goals is starting to look less like a bad night and more like the ceiling.

Puckline's Report

The Battle of Alberta lasted about one period. Mathieu Joseph scored at 7:46 of the first off a Connor McDavid feed, Mattias Ekholm made it 2-0 in the second, and then Edmonton scored twice in 21 seconds early in the third: Kasperi Kapanen on the power play and Alex Formenton right behind him. McDavid and Ryan Nugent-Hopkins had two assists each, and Tristan Jarry stopped all 24 shots for the shutout. Calgary tried a goalie change after the first, with Devin Cooley (8 saves on 9) giving way to Dustin Wolf (20 on 23), which fixed nothing because the problem was at the other end. Ty Emberson and Brennan Othmann dropped the gloves in the first. Edmonton is 9-2-2. Calgary is 5-7-0 and used two goalies and zero goals, which is a lot of equipment for a night with nothing to show for it.

Puckline's Report

Connor Brown scored both New Jersey goals, including an unassisted shorthanded one in the first, and the Devils still got run over 5-2 in Denver. Colorado scored five straight: Gabriel Landeskog tied it on the power play in the second, then Nazem Kadri, Parker Kelly, Nathan MacKinnon and Jaden Schwartz piled on in the third, the last two 30 seconds apart. Brent Burns and Sam Malinski had two assists each, and Kadri and Schwartz had a goal and an assist. The Avalanche outshot New Jersey 44-22; Jake Allen made 39 saves, Mackenzie Blackwood 20. Colorado is 7-5-1. New Jersey is 8-5-0, and after trading for a Vezina goalie last week, the 44 shots suggest the next phone call should be about the defense.

Puckline's Report

Toronto did the hard part and then forgot to finish. Down 4-2 in the third, the Leafs got one from Jack Roslovic and a 6-on-5 tying goal from Auston Matthews with 1:30 left, and then Brandon Montour won it for Seattle with 33 seconds to go, 5-4. Gavin McKenna had his first two-goal game, both on the power play, plus an assist; Matthews had a goal and two assists. Seattle spread it around: Berkly Catton, Josh Mahura with his first of the season, Chandler Stephenson on the power play, Ryker Evans and Montour, with Mackie Samoskevich adding two assists. Sergei Bobrovsky stopped 12 of 17; Philipp Grubauer 18 of 22. Cale Fleury and Vinni Lettieri fought in the second. Seattle is 8-4-1. Toronto is 7-6-2 and erased a two-goal deficit only to lose in the last minute, which is the most Maple Leafs sentence ever written.

WPG @ TBL · 7:00 PM ET

Winnipeg JetsWPG4-5-3 · 11 PTSML +180
@7:00 PM ETThu Oct 29 · Benchmark International Arena
WPG +180MLTBL -220
Tampa Bay LightningTBL7-3-1 · 15 PTSML -220

Puckline Preview

Winnipeg arrives in Tampa 0-4-2 in its last six with 10 goals in that stretch, and trading Connor Hellebuyck to New Jersey hasn't lifted the mood: the Jets now run a goalie timeshare, and the power play has failed on 14 straight chances over five games. Scott Arniel says he's not in panic mode but wants to split up the Mark Scheifele-Kyle Connor top line, which is usually what a coach says one week before panic mode. Connor still has nine goals, so at least somebody's working. This also starts a back-to-back for the Jets, who are in Florida on Friday.

Tampa is 5-0-0 at home, and Nikita Kucherov just passed Steven Stamkos as the franchise's all-time points leader, though the Lightning's last two were a loss in Colorado and a blown 4-2 lead in a 5-4 overtime loss in Utah. Brandon Hagel, tied for the team lead with seven goals, missed two practices, but Jon Cooper says he'll play tonight; Zemgus Girgensons is out. Victor Hedman left the Oct. 23 game after one shift and sat in Utah, but he's good to go tonight, and Andrei Vasilevskiy starts in goal. Last season the teams split, each winning 4-1 at home.

By Puckline Prince

UTA @ PIT · 7:00 PM ET

Utah MammothUTA8-5-0 · 16 PTSML -140
@7:00 PM ETThu Oct 29 · PPG Paints Arena
UTA -140MLPIT +116
Pittsburgh PenguinsPIT5-6-1 · 11 PTSML +116

Puckline Preview

Ten days ago these two played a 5-4 track meet in Utah that Sebastian Cossa saved with a pad stop on Ben Kindel in the final seconds. Clayton Keller and Nick Schmaltz each had a goal and an assist that night, and the last three meetings have all been one-goal games. The rematch opens a six-game road trip for Utah, which comes in hot under the collar: Tuesday's 3-1 loss to Minnesota had three early fights and 29 penalty minutes for Utah, and Keller's abuse-of-officials minor set up the Wild's winner. The Mammoth came in with the league's best power play and went 0-for-4, which is what happens when you spend the night defending one.

Pittsburgh has won two straight, a 4-0 shutout of Florida for Arturs Silovs and an overtime win over Nashville, and is 4-1-0 in its last five at home. Dan Muse says Kindel, Egor Chinakhov and Evgeni Malkin are all back tonight, while Samuel Girard is a game-time decision and Bryan Rust is still weeks away. Meanwhile TSN's Darren Dreger says Kyle Dubas is listening on Erik Karlsson, Kris Letang, Rust and Rickard Rakell. Karlsson leads the Penguins with 12 points, 11 of them assists, so he's doing his part to raise his own asking price.

CBJ @ CAR · 7:00 PM ET

Columbus Blue JacketsCBJ5-5-0 · 10 PTSML +205
@7:00 PM ETThu Oct 29 · Lenovo Center
CBJ +205MLCAR -255
Carolina HurricanesCAR10-2-2 · 22 PTSML -255

Puckline Preview

Carolina is 10-2-2, and Pyotr Kochetkov is 8-0-0, tying Frederik Andersen's franchise record for a season-opening win streak. He worked from the starter's crease at the morning skate, so he looks set to go for a ninth straight win instead of handing the net to Brandon Bussi, which is the kind of problem 31 other teams would like to have. Sebastian Aho has 19 points in 14 games, and his late goal beat Boston 2-1 on Tuesday, his 69th career game-winner and a franchise record.

Columbus comes in on two straight overtime wins, and that's the good news. The rest: the Blue Jackets have scored the fewest goals in the NHL, their power play ranks 30th, and they haven't won in regulation since opening night. On Tuesday they led Philadelphia 3-0, let the Flyers tie it with 11 seconds left, and needed Kent Johnson's overtime winner on a 2-on-0 to bail them out. Johnson leads the team with 10 points. Columbus is third in the league on faceoffs, so it should at least have the puck for the first two seconds of every shift. Last season Carolina won three of the four meetings, the latest 5-1 in Raleigh in April.

CHI @ DET · 7:30 PM ET

Chicago BlackhawksCHI4-8-0 · 8 PTSML +130
@7:30 PM ETThu Oct 29 · Little Caesars Arena
CHI +130MLDET -156
Detroit Red WingsDET5-4-3 · 13 PTSML -156

Puckline Preview

Patrick Kane goes back to Detroit in the other sweater. After three seasons as a Red Wing he signed for two years and $16 million with Chicago, leads the Blackhawks with eight points and is one assist from 900. Alex DeBrincat, his teammate in both cities, called facing him strange but fun. Chicago coach Jeff Blashill used to run Detroit's bench too, so this has the feel of a reunion where everybody brought an ex. The Hawks are 4-8-0, 0-4 on the road, and scored just enough to snap a three-game skid with a 2-1 win over Los Angeles on Tuesday. Bowen Byram travelled with the team but is listed injured and out of the projected lineup, and Alex Vlasic missed the morning skate with an illness and is a game-time decision.

Detroit is 4-1-1 in its last six, and Michal Postava stopped Connor McDavid and Leon Draisaitl in Monday's shootout win in Edmonton. Then there's Dylan Larkin: his trade request still stands, and after Wednesday's "maintenance day" he skipped the morning skate too. Todd McLellan says Larkin won't play tonight and left the explanation to interim GM Shawn Horcoff, while Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman reports Larkin won't play again until he's traded. Emmitt Finnie is projected to centre the top line in his place. Last season each team won in the other's building.

BOS @ STL · 8:00 PM ET

Boston BruinsBOS9-3-1 · 19 PTSML -110
@8:00 PM ETThu Oct 29 · Enterprise Center
BOS -110MLSTL -110
St Louis BluesSTL5-6-1 · 11 PTSML -110

Puckline Preview

The Blues haven't scored in 123 minutes and 55 seconds. They were shut out 4-0 by Carolina, then put 46 shots on Jacob Fowler on Tuesday and lost 2-0 anyway, their first back-to-back shutouts since November 2018. Jim Montgomery, who coached the Bruins until they fired him in November 2024, answered by reshuffling his top nine at practice and dropping Dylan Holloway to the third line, a bold way to treat a guy tied for the team lead with 10 points. Robert Thomas's next assist passes Brian Sutter for fourth on the Blues' all-time list, assuming someone on the Blues scores.

Boston leads the Atlantic at 9-3-1, though its eight-game point streak ended Tuesday with a 2-1 loss in Carolina on a season-low 16 shots. David Pastrnak leads the Bruins with 18 points, and Elias Lindholm has 17 points in 26 career games against St. Louis. Upstairs, Jeremy Jacobs handed the Bruins' governor seat to his son Charlie on Wednesday after 51 years. Boston won both meetings last season, both by the same 5-2 score.

WSH @ NSH · 8:00 PM ET

Washington CapitalsWSH7-4-0 · 14 PTSML -110
@8:00 PM ETThu Oct 29 · Bridgestone Arena
WSH -110MLNSH -110
Nashville PredatorsNSH4-3-5 · 13 PTSML -110

Puckline Preview

This is Alex Ovechkin's last regular-season game in Nashville, and the Predators have been his piggy bank: 20 goals and 32 points in 31 career games against them, 11 goals in 16 at Bridgestone Arena, four two-goal games and somehow never a hat trick. Before puck drop, Barry Trotz goes into the Predators' Golden Hall. He coached Nashville's first 15 seasons, then went to Washington and won the 2018 Cup with Ovechkin, so both benches owe him a thank-you card. The Capitals are 7-4-0 after Wednesday's 5-2 win over Philadelphia, with Alex Tuch and Jordan Kyrou scoring twice each. This is the back half of a back-to-back, so Charlie Lindgren is the likely starter, though nobody has confirmed it.

Nashville is 4-3-5, which means the Predators are 0-0-5 in games that go past regulation. On Tuesday they came back from 3-0 down against the Islanders and lost the shootout anyway, a whole comeback for a participation ribbon. Steven Stamkos leads them with 15 points. In the background, David Pagnotta reports Chicago, Calgary, Seattle and Philadelphia are interested in Washington's Ivan Miroshnichenko. Last season the teams split, each winning at home.

By Puckline Prince

MTL @ DAL · 8:00 PM ET

Montreal CanadiensMTL7-3-2 · 16 PTSML +155
@8:00 PM ETThu Oct 29 · American Airlines Center
MTL +155MLDAL -188
Dallas StarsDAL7-4-1 · 15 PTSML -188

Puckline Preview

Montreal rolls into Dallas 7-3-2 on a three-game winning streak, and it's doing it without Nick Suzuki, Ivan Demidov or Samuel Montembeault. Jacob Fowler earned a night off by stopping 46 shots for a shutout in St. Louis on Tuesday, his sixth straight win, so Martin St-Louis is giving the net to Jakub Dobes. Dobes's last start against Dallas was in November 2025, when he allowed the first five goals of a 7-0 Stars win, so he'll want a better sequel. The last game in Dallas went Montreal's way, 4-3 in overtime on Lane Hutson's goal in January. The Canadiens also take the second-most penalties in the league, which shows a lot of faith in their penalty kill.

Dallas allows a league-best 2.0 goals a game but ranks 25th in scoring, so nobody should book this one as a shootout. The Stars' five-game win streak ended Tuesday with a 5-1 home loss to New Jersey in Connor Hellebuyck's Devils debut, and the injury list keeps growing: Kyle Capobianco is now out four weeks, joining Esa Lindell, Radek Faksa and Matt Duchene, so call-up Trey Taylor makes his NHL debut on defense. Sam Steel returns after missing two games. Mikko Rantanen leads Dallas with 14 points.

By Puckline Prince

NYI @ MIN · 8:00 PM ET

New York IslandersNYI6-4-2 · 14 PTSML +158
@8:00 PM ETThu Oct 29 · Grand Casino Arena
NYI +158MLMIN -192
Minnesota WildMIN9-3-2 · 20 PTSML -192

Puckline Preview

Kirill Kaprizov has 14 goals in 14 games, the most in the NHL, and Quinn Hughes has 18 points, the most among defensemen. The Wild are 9-3-2, first in the Central and 4-0-0 at home. The only thing not running smoothly in Minnesota is the paperwork: GM Bill Guerin told WCCO he hasn't talked contract with Hughes' camp "in a long time" and hasn't decided whether Hughes, a free agent next July, stays all season. Nothing says first place like a GM who won't rule out trading his best defenseman. The blue line is already thin, with Brock Faber on IR, and now captain Jared Spurgeon is out week to week after blocking two shots in Utah, so David Spacek is expected to step in.

The Islanders finish a three-game Central trip with points in six of their last seven. Matthew Schaefer has a five-game point streak, Brayden Schenn scored his 300th career goal on Tuesday, and Semyon Varlamov won for the first time since November 2024, in a shootout after New York blew a 3-0 lead. Mathew Barzal, Matias Maccelli and Alexander Romanov are still out. Last season's game in St. Paul was an Islanders comeback: down 1-0, 2-1 and 3-2, they won 4-3 in overtime on Simon Holmstrom's second goal of the night.

By Puckline Prince

BUF @ ANA · 10:00 PM ET

Buffalo SabresBUF5-4-3 · 13 PTSML -142
@10:00 PM ETThu Oct 29 · Honda Center
BUF -142MLANA +116
Anaheim DucksANA5-6-1 · 11 PTSML +116

Puckline Preview

Last March in Anaheim, Troy Terry scored twice, including a breakaway winner 1:29 into overtime, as the Ducks won 6-5 and ended both Alex Lyon's 10-game road winning streak and Buffalo's seven-game road win streak. Terry is still out after hip surgery, though Joel Quenneville says he's getting close. Anaheim is 5-6-1 and found a new way to lose on Tuesday: up 4-1 on a Vancouver team that hadn't won in 10 games, beaten 6-5 in overtime on a 5-on-3. A.J. Greer scored twice in the loss, and Leo Carlsson leads the Ducks with 15 points.

Buffalo (5-4-3) had a goalie question, and the hot hand answered it. Colten Ellis stopped all 23 shots in Tuesday's 2-0 win in San Jose, which ended a three-game skid, and he's expected to start again tonight, while Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen sits at .866 over nine games. Zach Benson's empty-netter in San Jose was his first goal of the season, right after he was moved up next to Tage Thompson, and Jiri Kulich didn't make the California trip. Jack Quinn leads the Sabres with 11 points. Buffalo has also lost three games past regulation already, so it's had plenty of practice at almost.

OTT @ LAK · 10:00 PM ET

Ottawa SenatorsOTT8-5-0 · 16 PTSML -120
@10:00 PM ETThu Oct 29 · Crypto.com Arena
OTT -120MLLAK +100
Los Angeles KingsLAK3-6-2 · 8 PTSML +100

Puckline Preview

The Kings are 3-6-2 and haven't won at home yet, so tonight's start of a seven-game homestand is less a homecoming than an intervention. They went 3-2 on a five-game trip that ended with a 2-1 loss in Chicago, where Anton Forsberg stopped 25 of 27 and got one goal of support for his trouble. Drew Doughty and Corey Perry both sat in Chicago, but both skated this morning and Peter Laviolette expects them to play, with Darcy Kuemper expected in goal. Kevin Fiala and Mats Zuccarello are out, and Artemi Panarin leads Los Angeles with 11 points.

Ottawa (8-5-0) is on game two of a five-game trip and still without Linus Ullmark, who is expected to miss at least another week. Jonas Johansson gets his third straight start after beating the Rangers 7-4 behind a Drake Batherson hat trick and losing 4-1 in Vegas, where Warren Foegele was hurt on a knee-on-knee hit. Captain Thomas Chabot is back in the lineup after the Senators waived Cameron Crotty, and Carter Yakemchuk sits. Tim Stutzle leads Ottawa with 16 points. Last season the Kings won both meetings by one goal: 1-0 in Ottawa with former Senator Forsberg getting the shutout, and 2-1 in LA on Brandt Clarke's late power-play goal.

By Puckline Prince

VAN @ SJS · 10:00 PM ET

Vancouver CanucksVAN3-10-1 · 7 PTSML +140
@10:00 PM ETThu Oct 29 · SAP Center at San Jose
VAN +140MLSJS -170
San Jose SharksSJS6-6-1 · 13 PTSML -170

Puckline Preview

Vancouver finally won a hockey game. Down 4-1 in Anaheim on Tuesday, the Canucks scored four in the third, two of them from Jonathan Lekkerimaki 49 seconds apart, and won 6-5 in overtime on Filip Hronek's 5-on-3 goal, ending a 10-game winless run. All three Vancouver wins this season have been third-period comebacks, which is a thrilling way to be 3-10-1. Elias Pettersson treats San Jose like a stat-padding drill: 26 points in 26 career games against the Sharks, 15 points this season, and he just passed Alex Edler for eighth in Canucks career assists. Brock Boeser has 13 goals in 30 career games against San Jose.

The Sharks (6-6-1) got 38 saves from Yaroslav Askarov in Tuesday's 2-0 loss to Buffalo, his third straight game at .900 or better, while their top power-play unit managed one shot in a 90-second stretch. Filip Bystedt, a 2022 first-rounder, is set for his NHL debut between Kiefer Sherwood and Tyler Toffoli. Macklin Celebrini leads San Jose with 15 points. Last season the Sharks won the first three meetings before Vancouver took the last one in a shootout in April.

By Puckline Prince
